name: NASAMS

cost.display: AIM-120 AMRAAM interceptor ~$1.0-1.2M each; battery cost $91-428M depending on configuration

key_facts.label: Salvo / launcher
key_facts.value: networked, distributed launcher architecture (not single vehicle)

characteristics: networked, distributed launcher architecture (not single vehicle)
Strength: 94-100% reported intercept rate in Ukraine service; protected Kyiv early with strong results vs cruise missiles
Limitation: AMRAAM interceptor cost is high relative to drone/rocket threats it also gets tasked against
Estimated quantity available: Multiple batteries in service since 2022; exact current count not fully disclosed
employment_notes: One of the first Western SAMs credited with a 100% intercept rate defending Kyiv; validated distributed/networked SAM architecture as survivable under sustained bombardment
contrast_vs_traditional: Point-defense SAM doctrine like NASAMS' covered a handful of high-value fixed sites against a manned-aircraft or cruise-missile threat. A sky now also saturated with cheap one-way attack drones means density and layering matter as much as any single battery's range — the doctrine.md finding that soft-kill and hard-kill defenses have to stack together, not stand alone.

notes: Specs meet the bar but the unit cost is an estimate — cost is not verified.
